blogs.title: Heparin Before the Knife: How Pre‑Procedural UF Heparin Can Trigger Early Post‑Cardiac Surgery HIT
blogs.description: Examines the often missed priming effect of low‑dose unfractionated heparin given during pre‑operative cardiac catheterisation or other procedures on early onset heparin‑induced thrombocytopenia after cardiopulmonary bypass, reviews incidence data and timing windows (POD < 5), offers risk stratification tools for surgeons and intensivists, and proposes practical changes to perioperative platelet monitoring protocols to prevent this preventable complication.

blogs.title: Autoimmune HIT Unmasked: Clinical Clues That Distinguish It From Classic Heparin‑Dependent HIT
blogs.description: Delves into the spectrum of autoimmune (or “spontaneous”) HIT, highlighting hallmark findings such as precipitous platelet nadirs (<20 × 10⁹/L), thrombotic events out of proportion to modest thrombocytopenia, heparin‑independent platelet activation on functional assays, atypical timing relative to UF heparin exposure, and discusses how recognizing these patterns early alters management compared with conventional HIT.

blogs.title: When the Serotonin Release Assay Says ‘Indeterminate’: Spotting Partial FcγRIIa Blockade Resistance in Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: Provides a step‑by‑step guide for clinicians and laboratory personnel on interpreting atypical SRA results—strong serotonin release at zero heparin concentration and incomplete inhibition by the FcγRIIa blocking monoclonal antibody IV.3—explains the underlying immunologic mechanisms of partial Fc receptor blockade resistance seen in severe autoimmune HIT, and suggests decision pathways when functional testing yields ambiguous findings.

blogs.title: Therapeutic Anticoagulation in Severe Autoimmune HIT After Cardiopulmonary Bypass: Argatroban Versus Fondaparinux and Beyond
blogs.description: Compares direct thrombin inhibitors (argatroban, bivalirudin) with indirect factor Xa inhibitors (fondaparinux) and select DOACs for treating life‑threatening autoimmune HIT after cardiac surgery. Covers pharmacokinetic nuances (hepatic vs renal clearance), monitoring challenges amid recent stroke or bleeding risk, evidence from case series and guidelines, and presents an algorithm for switching agents when hypercoagulability persists despite initial therapy.

blogs.title: High‑Dose IVIG in Autoimmune HIT – Why Some Patients Fail to Bounce Back Quickly
blogs.description: Reviews the rationale behind high‑dose intravenous immunoglobulin as an adjunctive therapy for refractory autoimmune HIT—FcγR blockade leading to rapid platelet recovery—and analyzes why certain patients experience blunted responses despite adequate dosing. Discusses dosing schedules, timing relative to anticoagulation changes, alternative rescue strategies such as plasma exchange or complement inhibition.

blogs.title: Post‑CPB Thrombocytopenia Made Simple: A Practical Differential Diagnosis Algorithm for Surgeons and Intensivists
blogs.description: (Re)introduces an evidence‑based stepwise algorithm for evaluating platelet count drops after cardiopulmonary bypass. Covers common explanations (dilutional fall, surgical consumption), timeline clues differentiating early dilutional thrombocytopenia from late immune–mediated processes, recommended laboratory workup (peripheral smear review, coagulation profile, PF4 ELISA/SRA), criteria prompting workup for classic versus autoimmune HIT versus TTP/DIC/drug–induced ITP—all illustrated with key decision points drawn from the presented case.
